story: Alaska's Rural Health Transformation Program award list, opened and counted: 185 awards worth about $181.9 million, of which eight worth about $12.0 million buy a machine that reads, decides or flies

claims.claim: Alaska will receive $272,174,856 in the first year of the Rural Health Transformation Program.
claims.verbatim: Alaska will receive $272,174,856 in the first year
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
claims.notes: Corroborated independently by Country Journal, which prints '$272,174,856 for year one'. The same state page gives the exact federal award as $272,174,855.72 in a footer disclaimer, so the round number is the state's own rounding of its own figure.

claims.claim: The Rural Health Transformation Program is a $50 billion federal program covering all fifty states.
claims.verbatim: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) is a $50 billion federal opportunity to improve health care in rural areas across all fifty states.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Rural Health Transformation Program
claims.notes: The state page does not state the five-year term or the statute, so attribute any 'five-year' framing to Alaska Watchman and not to the state.

claims.claim: Alaska has announced 185 Rural Health Transformation Program project awards totalling about $182 million as of August 28th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Cumulative Total $182M Project Awards 185 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Read directly from the state's own summary PDF, page 1. Independently confirms the row count from the spreadsheet parse.

claims.claim: The 185 announced awards total $181,871,366.36 according to the state's own Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet.
claims.verbatim: PARSE ONLY. Not present as a string on any page fetched. State summary PDF rounds to $182M.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. Consistent with the state's published $182M rounding, and its four weekly components sum to it exactly. Deck says 'per the state's own award spreadsheet'. Prefer printing 'about $181.9 million'.

claims.claim: Alaska announced $4.5 million across 19 projects in the first weekly round on August 7th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Week 1 | Aug 7 $4.5M Project Awards 19 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Doubly corroborated. Country Journal reported 'over $4.5 million to 19 projects'. Parse gives $4,591,813.

claims.claim: Alaska announced $30.1 million across 37 projects in the second weekly round on August 14th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Week 2 | Aug 14 $30.1M Project Awards 37 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Parse gives $30,125,610, which rounds to the published $30.1M.

claims.claim: Alaska announced $130 million across 105 projects in the third weekly round on August 21st, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Week 3 | Aug 21 $130M Project Awards 105 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Largest single round, 57 percent of all announced money. FIVE of the eight machine awards fall in this round, not six. The fact-checker's draft said six and the showrunner re-counted from the spreadsheet's own notified-date column on 2026-08-30. The split is two on August 14th, five on August 21st, one on August 28th, and NONE on August 7th.

claims.claim: Alaska announced $16.9 million across 24 projects in the fourth weekly round on August 28th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Week 4 | Aug 28 $16.9M Project Awards 24 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Parse gives $16,862,504. The state PDF also shows a 'Weeks 5+' box marked TBA, so the award list is not closed.

claims.claim: The four announced weekly rounds sum to 185 projects, matching the state's published cumulative total.
claims.verbatim: 19 Projects ... 37 Projects ... 105 Projects ... 24 Projects ... 185 Projects
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Arithmetic re-derived on the state's own published counts. The parse's exact weekly dollars also sum to $181,871,366 to the cent.

claims.claim: The state says its award amounts are projected as of August 28th and that minor adjustments may still occur.
claims.value: Weeks 5 and beyond still to be announced
claims.verbatim: The data presented reflects projected award amounts as of August 28, and minor adjustments to award amounts may occur as the process is completed.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: THE HEDGE THE DECK CARRIES ON A SLIDE. Every dollar is preliminary. The spreadsheet column is headed 'Award Amount (Preliminary)'. Both the 185 count and the eight machine count are a snapshot, not a final tally.

claims.claim: Awards are being announced on a rolling weekly basis, on Fridays, across each of Alaska's 30 boroughs and census areas.
claims.verbatim: across each of Alaska's 30 boroughs and census areas. Project awards are being announced on a rolling weekly basis.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: The state's own program page says announcements began on Friday, August 7th and continue on a weekly basis, which is where the Friday cadence comes from.

claims.claim: Health Care Access is the largest initiative at $68.4 million, or 38 percent of announced funding.
claims.verbatim: Health Care Access ... $68.4M
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: The 38 percent is published on the state's own chart. Parse gives $68,432,700.

claims.claim: Spark Technology and Innovation received $32.6 million, or 18 percent of announced funding.
claims.verbatim: Spark Technology & Innovation ... $32.6M
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Five of the eight machine awards sit in this initiative. The state spells it two ways on one page, with an ampersand in the table and the word 'and' in the chart legend.

claims.claim: Pay for Value received $30.0 million, or 16 percent of announced funding.
claims.verbatim: Pay for Value ... $30.0M
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Parse gives $29,974,658.

claims.claim: Strengthen Workforce received $24.7 million, or 14 percent of announced funding.
claims.verbatim: Strengthen Workforce ... $24.7M
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: Parse gives $24,771,164.

claims.claim: Healthy Beginnings received $15.1 million and Healthy Communities received $10.7 million.
claims.verbatim: Healthy Beginnings ... $15.1M ... Healthy Communities ... $10.7M
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Alaska RHTP Year 1 Funding Cycle Update
claims.notes: 8 percent and 6 percent respectively. Parse gives $15,144,333 and $10,698,098.

claims.claim: Eight of the 185 awards have titles or summaries naming AI, robotics or drones, and they total $12,012,936 per the state's own award spreadsheet.
claims.verbatim: PARSE ONLY. Derived by summing eight award rows identified by keyword search of title and summary text.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE AND ON A STATED EDITORIAL DEFINITION. Arithmetic re-derived exactly. The count of eight is a keyword search, not a state category, and the deck says so in its own voice on the slide.

claims.claim: The eight awards are about 6.6 percent of all announced funding, or roughly one dollar in fifteen.
claims.verbatim: DERIVED. 12,012,936 divided by 181,871,366.36 equals 0.06605.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: PRINT 'about 6.6 percent', never 6.61, because the quotient sits on a rounding boundary and the inputs are preliminary. 181,871,366.36 divided by 12,012,936 equals 15.14, so one dollar in fifteen is sound.

claims.claim: A $6.5 million award brings the first robotic assisted minimally invasive surgery program to Southern Southeast Alaska.
claims.verbatim: $6.5 million to bring robotic-assisted, minimally invasive surgery to southern Southeast Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Watchman
claims.notes: DOUBLY CORROBORATED. Ermer Suter's Tuesday Report independently writes the same. Largest of the eight and 54 percent of the machine money. Parse gives $6,518,029.

claims.claim: The recipient of the $6.5 million robotic surgery award is PeaceHealth Ketchikan Medical Center, serving Ketchikan Gateway, Petersburg, Prince of Wales-Hyder and Wrangell.
claims.verbatim: PARSE ONLY. Row BP1-IA-254. No fetched page names the recipient.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: The MONEY and SUBSTANCE are doubly corroborated by press; the ORGANISATION NAME is parse-only. PeaceHealth's own site does not mention it. Source the name to the spreadsheet.

claims.claim: A $3.1 million award deploys AI powered medical imaging across 21 acute care hospitals for faster stroke detection.
claims.verbatim: more than $3.1 million to deploy AI-powered medical imaging across 21 acute care hospitals for faster stroke detection
claims.source_outlet: Ermer Suter, Tuesday Report
claims.notes: DOUBLY CORROBORATED. Alaska Watchman independently writes the same 21 hospital figure. The best sourced machine detail in the deck. Parse gives $3,156,626 to Alaska Stroke Coalition, statewide.

claims.claim: The AI imaging network runs on cloud based platforms using existing PACS without new imaging hardware, per the state's own award spreadsheet.
claims.verbatim: two complementary, cloud-based platforms that run on existing PACS without new imaging hardware
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. Explains how 21 hospitals are reached for $3.1 million. The organisation name Alaska Stroke Coalition is likewise parse-only.

claims.claim: A $250,000 planning award designs a drone based pharmaceutical delivery system for Interior Alaska villages.
claims.verbatim: $250,000 to develop a drone-based pharmaceutical delivery system for villages spread across 94,000 square miles, where medication deliveries can take five to 14 days during winter months
claims.source_outlet: Ermer Suter, Tuesday Report
claims.notes: DOUBLY CORROBORATED. Alaska Watchman independently confirms. Smallest headline number with the largest geography, which is the deck's best contrast.

claims.claim: The drone award covers 42 Interior Alaska villages across 94,000 square miles where medication delivery can take 5 to 14 days in winter.
claims.verbatim: villages spread across 94,000 square miles, where medication deliveries can take five to 14 days during winter months
claims.source_outlet: Ermer Suter, Tuesday Report
claims.notes: The 94,000 square miles and the 5 to 14 day delay are confirmed verbatim on a fetched page. The count of 42 villages, the Fairbanks hub and the recipient name Tanana Chiefs Conference are parse-only, row BP1-PL-026.

claims.claim: The drone planning project names ACUASI at the University of Alaska Fairbanks as its partner, and UAF is a lead participant in the FAA's BEYOND drone program.
claims.verbatim: University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, BEYOND program
claims.notes: FAA's own page lists UAF among BEYOND lead participants. Use the center's own name, ACUASI at UAF. ACUASI's site does not mention medical delivery, so do not imply it has flown medicine.

claims.claim: The FAA's BEYOND drone program logged 70,563 total flights, of which 48,383 were beyond visual line of sight.
claims.verbatim: BEYOND achieved 70,563 total flights; 48,383 of those flights took place beyond visual line of sight
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration, BEYOND program
claims.notes: PRIMARY AND CLEAN. These are cumulative figures for the whole national program, NOT Alaska only, and the deck must not imply otherwise.

claims.claim: An award of about $25,500 funds AI assisted clinical documentation at Kodiak Community Health Center.
claims.verbatim: use of AI-assisted clinical documentation. KCHC says the technology is intended to reduce the amount of time providers spend on documentation
claims.source_outlet: Kodiak Daily Mirror
claims.notes: The parse says $25,492 and the Mirror says $25,493, and the Mirror's five figures sum exactly to its stated total, so print 'about $25,500'. Smallest of the eight either way, and the smallness is the story.

claims.claim: The AI documentation project is one of five Kodiak Community Health Center awards totalling $657,688.
claims.verbatim: Kodiak Community Health Center has been awarded $657,688 in the second round of 2026 grants
claims.source_outlet: Kodiak Daily Mirror
claims.notes: Scale check for the deck. The AI piece is under 4 percent of what one clinic received.

claims.claim: A $430,000 award funds AI clinical documentation for behavioral health at Maniilaq Association across the North Slope and Northwest Arctic boroughs.
claims.verbatim: a remote roadless area in northwest Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. The application says the documentation burden 'has been cited as a driver of therapist turnover'. That is the applicant's own assertion, not a state finding, so the deck attributes it to the application.

claims.claim: A $250,000 award funds an AI assisted eight lead EEG headband at Mat-Su Regional Medical Center, intended to identify status epilepticus locally.
claims.verbatim: a single-use, eight-lead headband
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE, expected since it is in the August 28th round press had not yet covered. The avoided transfer into Anchorage is a projected benefit in an application, so phrase as 'intended to', never as an outcome.

claims.claim: Two further awards complete the eight, $1,241,086 to MapHabit for AI powered visual maps and $141,703 to the Statewide Independent Living Council for an AI assistive technology assessment tool.
claims.verbatim: MapHabit delivers AI-powered visual maps for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, traumatic brain injury, and Alzheimer's-related dementias.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. The fact-checker flagged MapHabit as soft because its TITLE carries no AI keyword. Re-read of row BP1-IA-200 resolves it: the summary says 'AI-powered visual maps' outright, so the row belongs in the eight. SILC's row BP1-IA-319 says 'artificial-intelligence assistive technology needs assessment tool'. Both statewide, both notified August 21st.

claims.claim: CMS was reported in late August to have announced $160 million for 142 Alaska health projects, a smaller count than the state's own 185.
claims.verbatim: CMS awarded Alaska $160 million through the Rural Health Transformation Program, funding 142 projects to expand access to rural healthcare statewide.
claims.source_outlet: Ermer Suter, Tuesday Report
claims.notes: REPORTED, NOT READ AT SOURCE. cms.gov returned 403 to three agents. Two outlets agree on the figures. USE ONLY IF ATTRIBUTED, and never as contradicting the state. Do not cite cms.gov as read.

claims.claim: Not one of the eight machine awards was notified in the first round on August 7th, 2026.
claims.value: zero of eight in round one
claims.verbatim: DERIVED from the notified-date column. Two on August 14th, five on August 21st, one on August 28th.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. Editorially this is the sharpest fact in the set, because August 7th is exactly the round carousel No.35 covered on 2026-08-16, and its deck reported that the first Friday bought X-ray machines, a hydroponic farm and a scheduling system. This claim says why. There was no machine in that round to find.

claims.claim: The eight awards name twelve distinct boroughs and census areas between them, plus three that are statewide.
claims.verbatim: DERIVED from the Service Area column. Ketchikan Gateway, Petersburg, Prince of Wales-Hyder, Wrangell, North Slope, Northwest Arctic, Matanuska-Susitna, Denali, Fairbanks North Star, Southeast Fairbanks, Yukon-Koyukuk, Kodiak Island.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Health, Notice of Intent to Award spreadsheet
claims.notes: RESTS ON THE PARSE ALONE. Every one of the twelve resolves to a named polygon in assets/geo/alaska-boroughs.geo.json, which is what the deck draws. North Slope appears in two awards and is counted once.

killed.claim: On August 27th and 28th, 2026 the FAA and USDOT announced BEYOND Phase 2, adding up to eight new lead participants, with proposals due September 10th, 2026.
killed.why: CONTRADICTED BY THE PRIMARY SOURCE. FAA's own BEYOND page says Phase 2 began in 2025 under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 and runs to 2029. It carries no August 2026 announcement, no new participant count and no September 10th deadline. The live deadline hook dies entirely. C27 and C28 carry the drone regulatory context without it.

killed.claim: The state's published summary counts 36 Spark projects, so the ampersand spelling in one row has a visible consequence in the state's own tally.
killed.why: THE PREMISE DOES NOT EXIST. The state's initiative table has three columns, Initiative, Description and Funding, and publishes no project counts at all. There is no published 36 or 37 to compare against. The state PDF also spells the initiative both ways on one page, so the spreadsheet variant is plausibly cosmetic. Dropped rather than hedged.

killed.claim: The eight machine awards are 6.61 percent of announced funding.
killed.why: ARITHMETIC OFF AT THE ROUNDING BOUNDARY. The true quotient is 6.6052 percent, which reaches 6.61 only under round-half-up, and the inputs are explicitly preliminary. Replaced by C18, about 6.6 percent and about one dollar in fifteen.

killed.claim: CMS announced $160 million for 142 Alaska projects, per cms.gov.
killed.why: PRIMARY SOURCE UNREACHABLE. cms.gov returned 403 to three separate agents. The substance survives only secondhand and is retained in that weaker form as C34. The cms.gov URL must not appear as though it were read.

killed.claim: PeaceHealth Ketchikan Medical Center confirms the robotic surgery expansion.
killed.why: NO AWARDEE CONFIRMATION EXISTS. PeaceHealth Ketchikan's own page makes no mention of robotic surgery or an RHTP grant. The award survives as C21 on two press reports plus the parse; only awardee confirmation is killed.
